transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, um… I came in because I’m starting to get really worried about mistakes I’m making at work. I’m a camera operator and editor, so a lot of my job is technical and detail-heavy, and I know how to do these things — that’s the part that’s been bothering me.

Lately I keep making these stupid mistakes, like labeling camera cards wrong, or missing a timecode note that I specifically meant to write down, or exporting a client cut and then realizing the lower-third is wrong even though I swear I checked it. And it’s not like I don’t understand the workflow. I do. I’ve been doing this long enough that these are things I should catch, and sometimes I even do a pass to check them and something still slips through.

I guess what finally scared me into making the appointment was feeling like, okay, this isn’t just “everyone makes mistakes sometimes.” It’s happening in ways that could really affect my work and how people see me professionally, and I’m tired of feeling like I can’t trust myself with basic details I know better than to miss.
Do you often find your mind drifting off when you’re trying to focus on a task?

I’m not totally sure, honestly. I mean, I know I can get pulled away from what I’m doing, but when you say “mind drifting off,” I’m not sure if you mean like daydreaming or kind of blanking out or just thinking about the next thing I have to do.

With editing, sometimes I’ll be looking right at the timeline and I’ll realize I’m not really tracking what I’m looking at anymore, but I don’t know if that’s my mind wandering or if it’s just fatigue or being overwhelmed by all the little pieces. It’s not always like I’m thinking about something pleasant or totally unrelated — sometimes it’s more like I lose the thread for a second and then have to back up and re-check where I was.

So… maybe? I’ve noticed that I can sort of slip off task, but I don’t know how often that is compared to normal.
Looking back to when you were a child in school, did you often have trouble paying attention or staying organized?

Yeah… looking back, I think there was definitely something there, though I don’t know if I would’ve described it as “paying attention” at the time.

In elementary school especially, I was always being moved around the classroom. Like, teachers would move my desk closer to them, or away from certain kids, because I was out of my seat a lot or talking to classmates when I wasn’t supposed to. I remember blurting out answers before I was called on — sometimes even when I did know I was supposed to raise my hand, it was like the answer came out before I had fully thought through the “wait your turn” part.

And bothering classmates… not in a mean way, I don’t think, but I’d be poking someone, whispering something, turning around, trying to show them something, and then I’d realize the teacher was watching me or that I had gotten someone else in trouble. It’s embarrassing to think about now because I remember feeling like I wasn’t trying to be a problem, but I kept doing things before I caught myself.

So yes, teachers noticed it pretty early. My desk got moved more than once because I couldn’t stay seated or quiet, basically.
As a child, did these kinds of problems happen at home too, or mainly just at school?

I’m not totally sure, honestly. I remember school more clearly because there were teachers commenting on it and moving my desk and things like that, so it’s easier to point to.

At home… I mean, I’m sure I was probably energetic and maybe hard to settle sometimes, but I don’t have a clean memory of, like, my parents saying the same kinds of things in a way that stands out. It wasn’t tracked or documented the same way, you know? At school it was obvious because there were rules and a whole classroom of kids, and if I was talking or getting up, it became a problem right away.

So I don’t want to say it only happened at school, because I honestly don’t know. I just don’t have as specific a memory of home being a major issue in the same way.
When you were a child, did these same difficulties ever cause problems in another setting besides school, like at home, with friends, or during activities?

I’m not really sure. I wish I had a clearer answer, because I know that’s probably important, but when I try to think back, the memories outside school are kind of fuzzy.

With school, it’s easy because there were teachers and desks being moved and specific moments where I got corrected. At home or with friends or activities, I don’t have the same kind of clear record in my head. I can imagine maybe it showed up there too, just because I was the same kid, but I don’t want to say yes if I’m only guessing.

I don’t remember, like, a specific ongoing problem at home or in an activity that stands out the way school does. So I guess my honest answer is: I don’t know. School is the setting I can really remember it causing problems in.
Do you spend a lot of your day worrying about different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to solve?

I’m not sure I’d describe myself that way, no. I mean, I do think about things, obviously — work stuff, scheduling, whether I forgot something, normal life things — but I don’t know that I spend a lot of the day worrying in that kind of constant, spinning way.

When there’s an actual issue in front of me, I can get caught up in it, but if you mean worrying about lots of different things even when nothing is really happening, I don’t think that’s a main thing for me. At least it’s not something I’ve really noticed as taking over my day.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days lately?

I don’t think so, no — at least not in the sense of feeling depressed most days. I mean, I have normal ups and downs, and there are days where I’m tired or frustrated or kind of blah, especially if work has been a lot or I feel like I’m behind on things. But I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down in a persistent way lately.

I guess I’d separate it from stress or irritation, if that makes sense. I can get overwhelmed or annoyed, but it doesn’t usually feel like this heavy sadness that’s there day after day. So my answer would be no, not most days.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your work because you can’t shake the feeling that something might be wrong, even when it looks correct?

Not really, no. I mean, I check my work because in editing or camera-related work you kind of have to — like, you scrub through something, make sure the file exported properly, make sure the audio isn’t off, that sort of thing. But I don’t think it’s that I can’t shake a feeling that something is wrong when it looks fine.

If something is important, I might look it over more than once, but it feels practical, not like I’m trapped in checking it over and over. Once I can see it’s okay, I can usually move on. I don’t think that repeated-checking feeling is a big thing for me.
Have these concentration and mistake problems gotten noticeably worse compared with how you functioned in the past?

Yes. That’s actually kind of what scared me into finally coming in, because it’s not like I don’t know how to do my job. I’ve been doing this long enough that certain things should be automatic, and lately I keep making these dumb technical mistakes that I know better than to make.

Like, I’ll label camera cards wrong, or miss a timecode note that I really should have caught, or I’ll export a client cut and then realize the lower-third is the wrong version even though I swear I checked it. And those are the kinds of things where, in the past, I might have made a mistake once in a while because everyone does, but now it feels more noticeable and embarrassing. It’s not that I don’t care — if anything, I’m trying hard to be careful — but somehow these little details are slipping through anyway.

So yes, compared with how I used to function, it does feel worse, or at least more frequent and harder to brush off.
Have you been having trouble with your memory lately?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, because I don’t feel like I’m forgetting big things, if that’s what you mean. Like I’m not getting lost or forgetting people’s names in some major way, or anything like that.

I do sometimes feel like little things slip out of my head, but it’s hard for me to tell whether that’s “memory” exactly or just… I didn’t register it properly in the first place. Like if someone tells me something while I’m in the middle of doing three other things, I might later be like, “Wait, did you say that was today or tomorrow?” But I don’t know if that counts as memory trouble or more just not fully taking it in.

So I guess I’d say I haven’t noticed a serious memory problem lately. It’s more that I can be scattered, and then it looks like I forgot something. But if you mean actual memory, I’m not sure I’d describe it that way.
How old are you?
I’m 38. Well, I turned 38 recently-ish — I always have to think for a second now because after the mid-thirties they kind of blur together, but yeah, 38.
Have you started using any new medication or substances around the time these concentration problems got worse?

Not that I can think of, no. I mean, I’ve been trying to think about that because it would be kind of easier if there were some obvious explanation, like, “Oh, I started taking this thing and then everything got worse,” but I can’t point to anything like that.

I haven’t noticed a new medication or some new substance lining up with when the concentration issues got more obvious. At least nothing is jumping out at me. I guess if you mean something really broad, like supplements or changes in caffeine or anything like that, I’d have to think about it more carefully, but there hasn’t been some clear new thing that I started where I was like, “Oh, this changed my brain.”
Outside of work, do these same attention or detail problems cause trouble in your daily life?

I’m not sure how much it causes actual trouble outside of work. I mean, I definitely notice I can be scattered in everyday stuff, but I’m trying not to overstate it because it’s not like there’s one huge example popping into my head where my life fell apart because I missed a detail.

It’s more like… I’ll sometimes have to double-check things or I’ll realize I wasn’t really paying attention to something someone said, but I don’t know if that’s the same kind of problem you’re asking about. Outside work there’s also less pressure for everything to be exact, so it doesn’t always stand out to me in the same way.

So I guess my honest answer is: maybe a little, but I’m not totally sure. I haven’t really tracked it closely in my daily life.
In your home life, do these attention or detail problems cause noticeable problems?

At home… I’m honestly not totally sure. I mean, I notice little things sometimes, like I’ll be doing something and then realize I’ve sort of lost the thread, or I’ll have to go back and check whether I actually did something or just thought about doing it. But I don’t know if I’d call it a noticeable “problem,” exactly.

It’s different than work because at work there are clearer consequences if I miss a detail, you know? At home, if I’m a little scattered, sometimes it just gets absorbed into the day. Like it’s annoying, maybe, or it makes things take longer, but I’m not sure I can point to some big home-life issue and say, “Yes, that’s definitely because of attention or detail problems.”

So… maybe mildly, but I haven’t really been tracking it that way. I’d have to think more about what counts as noticeable.
Has anyone you live with complained about your being forgetful, disorganized, or not following through on things at home?

I’m not sure, honestly. I can’t think of someone making a clear complaint like, “You never follow through,” or “You’re always disorganized,” in a way that’s stuck with me.

I mean, little comments happen in normal household life, right? Like someone might ask, “Did you do that thing?” and I’ll realize I’m not sure, or I meant to and then got sidetracked. But I don’t know if I’d call that a pattern of complaints, or just regular day-to-day stuff. I’m trying to separate what’s actually been said from what I’m imagining they might be frustrated by, if that makes sense.

So I guess my answer is: not that I’ve really noticed as a repeated complaint. If it’s happening, it hasn’t been brought up to me in a big or direct way.
Has a romantic partner ever told you that you seem forgetful, disorganized, or easily distracted at home?

I’m trying to think… I don’t know that a romantic partner has said it to me in that exact way, like, “You’re forgetful” or “You’re disorganized at home.” Not as a clear, repeated complaint that I can point to.

There may have been moments where someone was annoyed because I didn’t catch something they said, or I forgot to circle back to something we’d talked about, but I’m not sure if that was framed as a pattern or just normal relationship friction. I don’t want to turn every little comment into evidence of something if it wasn’t really meant that way.

So I guess I’d say… not that I specifically remember. If they noticed it, it wasn’t something that was brought up to me in a really direct or memorable way.
Have you been getting enough sleep lately?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, because “enough” kind of depends on the week for me. Lately I don’t think I’ve been tracking it very carefully. Some nights I feel like I probably got a reasonable amount, and other mornings I wake up and I’m like, okay, maybe that wasn’t quite enough, but I haven’t been writing it down or anything.

I wouldn’t want to give you a number and make it sound more precise than it is. I guess I’d say my sleep has been… somewhat variable? Not something I’ve really focused on as the main issue, but also not something I can confidently say is perfect.
On most nights lately, how many hours of sleep have you been getting?

I honestly don’t know exactly. I’m trying to estimate, and it’s not like I’m checking the clock every night in a consistent way. If I had to guess, on a lot of nights it’s probably somewhere around… maybe six-ish? But I don’t feel confident saying that like it’s a measured number.

Some nights I might be closer to seven, and other nights it feels like less, but I’m kind of piecing that together from when I remember going to bed and when I remember waking up, which isn’t always accurate. So I’d say I don’t have a solid number, but it doesn’t feel like a totally regular, predictable amount every night.
When you get a full night of sleep, do your attention problems improve?

I mean… maybe a little, but not enough that I can say sleep explains it. Like if I get a really solid night, I might feel less foggy in the morning, sure, but the mistakes I’m worried about still happen even when I’m not exhausted.

What really scared me into coming in is that I’ve been making these dumb technical mistakes at work that I absolutely know better than to make. I work with camera footage and edits, so it’ll be things like labeling camera cards wrong, or missing a timecode note, or exporting a client cut and somehow the wrong lower-third is still in there even though I swear I checked it. And those are not things where I’m like, “Oh, I don’t know how to do this.” I do know. That’s what makes it feel so awful.

So, yes, I think sleep affects the edges of it, maybe, but getting a full night doesn’t make me suddenly careful and consistent. I still have these moments where something slips past me, and then afterward I’m just standing there thinking, how did I miss that?
Outside of work, do you often misplace everyday things like your keys, wallet, or phone?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think of myself as someone who’s constantly losing my keys or wallet in some dramatic way, but I also don’t know if I’m the best judge of that because I have little places where I try to put things, and if I actually use those places then it’s fine.

My phone… I mean, everybody misplaces their phone sometimes, right? I’ll set it down while I’m doing something else and then have that little moment of, wait, where did I just put it? But I don’t know that I’d say it’s a major outside-of-work problem, at least not one I’ve been paying close attention to. Keys and wallet, I haven’t really noticed a big pattern there. It’s more like occasional normal-life stuff, as far as I can tell.
